title: Pfizer Earnings Beat Estimates as Eliquis Growth Offsets COVID Decline, Guidance Raised
excerpt: Third-quarter revenue of $16.58 billion and adjusted EPS of $0.87 topped consensus, and Pfizer lifted its full-year revenue outlook by $1.5 billion at the midpoint.
body:
• Pfizer reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $16.58 billion, essentially flat from $16.65 billion a year earlier, and adjusted diluted earnings per share of $0.87, unchanged from a year ago — ahead of the Zacks consensus estimates of $16.13 billion in revenue and $0.72 in earnings per share.
  • Growth outside COVID products did the work: revenue excluding Comirnaty and Paxlovid rose 7% operationally, and recently launched and acquired products grew 32% operationally to $3.8 billion, led by Eliquis, Padcev and Nurtec.
  • Pfizer raised its full-year 2026 guidance: revenue is now expected at $62.0 billion to $64.0 billion, up $1.5 billion at the midpoint, and adjusted diluted EPS at $2.95 to $3.05, up from $2.80 to $3.00.
  • For shareholders, Pfizer returned $7.3 billion in cash dividends in the first nine months of 2026, while reported net income fell 8% to $3.24 billion as COVID sales kept shrinking.

Pfizer beat Wall Street expectations for the third quarter and raised its full-year outlook on Tuesday, as strong sales of blood thinner Eliquis and newer cancer and migraine medicines offset the continuing decline of its COVID-19 vaccine and antiviral pill.

The numbers, reported versus expected

Revenue for the quarter ended in September was $16.58 billion, compared with $16.65 billion in the same quarter of 2025, according to Pfizer's third-quarter release. That was ahead of the $16.13 billion Zacks Consensus Estimate, a positive surprise of 2.8%, Zacks reported. Adjusted diluted earnings per share held at $0.87, the same as a year earlier, but above the $0.72 consensus estimate — an earnings surprise of 20.83%, according to Zacks. On a reported basis, diluted earnings per share fell 9% to $0.56 from $0.62, and reported net income declined 8% to $3.24 billion.

The adjusted figure includes a one-time $650 million research charge tied to Pfizer's agreement with Innovent Biologics, estimated at about $0.10 per share — one reason adjusted earnings held steady while reported earnings fell.

Where the growth came from

The mix underneath the flat headline changed considerably. Eliquis generated $2.52 billion worldwide, up about 25% and ahead of analyst estimates, driven mainly by a higher U.S. net price and higher global demand, the company said. Padcev, its bladder cancer treatment, rose 55% operationally, the Vyndaqel family grew 12% operationally to $1.77 billion worldwide, according to Zacks' product-sales compilation, Nurtec rose 33% operationally and lung cancer drug Lorbrena rose 43%.

Those gains were largely absorbed by the COVID franchise. Paxlovid revenue fell 63% operationally to $449 million as infection rates declined globally, and Comirnaty vaccine revenue fell 29% operationally to $808 million, which Pfizer attributed in part to narrower vaccine recommendations and lower U.S. use. The Prevnar pneumonia vaccine family also declined 10% operationally. The net effect: Pfizer's non-COVID business grew while the overall top line stood still.

Guidance raised, new CFO in place

Management raised its full-year 2026 guidance for both measures. Revenue guidance moved to $62.0 billion to $64.0 billion, from $60.5 billion to $62.5 billion previously. Adjusted diluted earnings guidance was raised and narrowed to $2.95 to $3.05, from $2.80 to $3.00. Pfizer said the increase reflects strong year-to-date performance and progress on cost programs, and already absorbs the Innovent charge.

"Pfizer had another strong quarter with commercial momentum and disciplined execution while advancing our strategy for creating long-term shareholder value," Chairman and Chief Executive Albert Bourla said in the release. Cecile Guegan, who took over as chief financial officer on November 1, said the quarter reflected "strong commercial performance globally and continued operational discipline."

Capital and what to watch

Pfizer said it invested $8.3 billion in internal research and development in the first nine months of 2026 and returned $7.3 billion in dividends, or $1.29 per share. It completed no share repurchases in 2026 and expects none under current guidance.

Investors were cautious despite the beat: Pfizer shares closed down 2.19% at $30.00 on Tuesday, according to The Motley Fool, which noted Eliquis's growth leaned heavily on U.S. price rather than volume, with a Medicare negotiated price now in effect for 2026. What to watch next is whether that pricing holds, and whether the non-COVID portfolio can return total revenue to growth when Pfizer reports full-year results.
